rubric_notes: Complete. Verified release record, a.22/a.22.1, homology endpoint (sf, no warnings), five families with sunids, example domains (d1f1ea_, d2bykb1, d1r4va_), linker histone a.4.5.13 lineage with sunids. Correct remote-homology framing, refuses function/interface/DNA-contact transfer, honest that HU/IHF classification was not checked and that SIDs are illustrations not quality-ranked representatives. Correctly avoids claiming independent origin for H1/H5. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineages with sunids, boundaries and annotations all in bundle. Deepest shared level identified as superfamily, interpreted as probable remote homology; fold alone noted as insufficient. Rejects HisE/MazG function transfer, treats Li/UNL as non-evidence, requires alignment for template use, notes 7-93 boundary. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Families, superfamily, fold, class, sunids, duplication comment, homology record and the full list of c.55 superfamilies all match the evidence bundle. Infers remote homology and the shared two-lobe RNase H-like core with cleft ATP binding and hinge closure; explicitly refuses transfer of substrate, reaction, ligand, regulation, partner, cellular role; notes fold membership is not a positive homology claim nor proof of convergence. Honest about mechanistic details coming from general knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All cited facts supported by bundle including homology endpoint. Correct superfamily/family/fold semantics, divergent chemistry on shared scaffold, explicit unsafe transfers including within-family, evidence required (sequence/structure hits, conserved ligands, biochemistry), caveat on automated matches. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct families and sunids in b.6.1, lineage, comments, Pfam xrefs and homology records (no warnings) verified against bundle. Separates family versus superfamily meaning, treats superfamily as probable distant homology, explicitly refuses copper binding and electron transfer for ephrin and PAD4 and the reverse, requires ligand residues plus experimental metal/redox data, and advises same-family templates. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct hierarchy (d.15.1.1/.2/.5 under d.15.1, fold d.15, class d) with sunids all matching the bundle; d1ubqa_/d1rfaa_ deepest shared node = superfamily is supported by the parents endpoints, and empty homology warnings are supported. Superfamily framed as probable common ancestry beyond fold; explicit rejection of transferring conjugation, p97 binding and Ras binding across families; notes different superfamily is not proof of analogy; separates background knowledge from SCOPe-verified facts and names needed external evidence. All must_include met, no must_avoid violated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, fold description, release and homology-endpoint statements all supported by bundle. Correctly frames remote superfamily homology vs fold-only similarity, notes different superfamilies do not prove non-homology, rejects phosphorylation, two-component, catalytic and generic function transfer, and template interchangeability. Uses SCOPe's 'lacks canonical receiver domains features' comment appropriately. Domain recruitment covered via catalysis in other ODC domains and KaiA clock role not inferable from CheY.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy, sunids, d3a5ca3 boundaries (3a5c A:113-184), PubMed 19893485, 'complexed with adp' note and homology scope all supported by bundle. Fold vs superfamily distinction correct, within-superfamily/family homology claim stated, explicit that separate superfamily is not evidence of convergence; unsafe transfers and missing external evidence named. The 3a5c four-domain split and 2.07 presence claims are not in this answer's bundle but are correct SCOPe facts; noted, not penalized.

All identifiers, release, fold comment, and homology warning supported by bundle. Correct fold-vs-superfamily inference, explicitly rejects both merging and the unrelated/convergent conclusion, limits function and template transfer, and names sequence HMM, structural heme-ligand alignment, and literature evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct hierarchy with sunids, homology record, family comment and Pfam mapping supported by bundle; protein lists for c.2.1.8/c.2.1.9 match. Superfamily = probable homology stronger than fold; separate families = not close relatives; usefully notes SCOPe does not resolve sub-relationships among the families. Bars transfer of mechanism, ligand specificity, oligomer state, binding residues; domain-boundary caveat; warns against calling other Rossmann-like folds non-homologous. Minor imprecision in describing the c.2.1.9 'assignment' as an automated Pfam mapping (the comment records a Pfam cross-mapping, not the family placement). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage, sunids, ligand comments and protein-level split, all supported. Calibrated interpretation and good limits (no function/metal transfer, exclude from benchmarks, flags own interpretation). However it states no explicit warning was retrieved and derives the caveat only from class-k semantics; the family 100905 'not a true family' annotation was never retrieved or cited.

All must_include met and bundle-supported: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 own fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 sharing c.23.14; sunid continuity; superfamily rename; tag domains identified as not part of biological reclassification. Correct evolutionary interpretation (shared superfamily = probable common ancestry, much stronger than shared fold; separate families = not close) and explicit statement that 1.69 different-fold placement was never evidence of independent origin. Limits on function/template transfer and on unverified paper rationale; honest about not querying intermediates. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All must_include met: d1a14h2 H:1-8 as synthetic N-terminal tag in class l, l.1.1.1 (sunids match bundle); d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 VH; tag similarity explicitly rejected as homology evidence, with homology endpoint warning cited verbatim. Correctly distinguishes b.1.1 superfamily vs b.1 fold support. Honest limits (sequence 404, SEQRES start QVQLQQSG noted without over-interpreting). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Correct whole-chain 1.75 assignment with lineage sunids, unchanged in 2.03, split first appearing in 2.04 and identical through 2.08 with both sids, sunids, boundaries and sccs. Uses the PA14-like superfamily's GLEYA, GH31 and beta-glucosidase (Kluyveromyces marxianus) members as retrieved evidence that the N-terminal region is a reused module hidden by the former toxin-specific whole-chain family. Keeps superfamily ancestry distinct from function in both directions, states that separate superfamilies imply no positive ancestry claim rather than proven unrelatedness, calls boundaries revisable curated hypotheses, and gives per-domain, release-remapped search guidance including that a missing hit is not evidence of absence.

All must_include met with bundle-supported identifiers, boundaries, sccs, protein-node species history for c.55.3.14. Mosaic interpretation, superfamily = probable ancestry, no function transfer, new fold not proof of independent origin, different superfamilies not proof of non-homology, group II intron origin labeled as literature interpretation. Claim of no caveats for all five domains slightly exceeds bundle (a1 only) but matches other bundles and is immaterial. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: all three in a.298.1.1, length attributed to repeat copy number and terminal segments, and the 're' heterogeneity flag plus the 34-residue canonical repeat 4cj9 A:259-292 with representative-only coordinates both used correctly. Strong limits: partial-coverage alignments are expected for repeat arrays and are not boundary errors, d2kq5a_ cannot template the superhelix, no RVD/target/role transfer, and it cleanly separates API-derived facts from background knowledge it did not verify. Lineage, lengths and comments match the evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata and periodic label. Cites stable 2.08 pinned in paths, rejects floating 'current', refuses to substitute the periodic label, and names the dated label if periodic-only data was used. Says the periodic update adds to 2.08 without replacing it and is not a new stable. But it declines to say what periodic updates contain (newly classified PDB entries, older stable domains untouched), so must_include item 3 is only partially covered.

Complete and well supported: 1.75 vs 2.08 comparison shows unchanged a.47.2.1 lineage but added 'ms' flag on d1br0a_/d1ez3a_; fragment comment cited; fold definition (four long helices) used to explain that three-helix fragments cannot show the fold and inherit it from the complete syntaxin domain; d1dn1b_ change from curated 17771 to automated match 302344 to d3c98b_ and curated d3c98b_ reference documented. Appropriate limits on homology (fold vs superfamily), function transfer, template use, and explicit statement that quality records were not retrieved. Only nit: 'New in 2.08' slightly overstates since intermediate releases were not checked, though it hedges by saying it was absent in 1.75. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Good inference: convergence signature across lineages, divergence only within superfamily/family, 'not a curated negative finding' caveat, deep-homology possibility vs convincing analogy (d.58.20 vs c.2), evidence needed beyond hierarchy. Uses the c.31.1 'opposite direction' annotation well. Minor imprecision: groups c.31 with c.2/c.3 as having 'similar binding modes' although it had just cited the annotation that c.31.1 binds cofactor in the opposite orientation, and the c.2 comment refers to c.3 and c.4. All sunids and annotations otherwise supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Precise and fully supported. Identifies the lowest shared node in 2.04 as class b with ColG in b.23.2 under CUB-like b.23 and Cry3A in b.18.1 under b.18, then the 2.05 move into new family b.18.1.36 with the fold changing as well, sunid and SID retained, and 2.08 shared superfamily with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 still separate. Correctly excludes the two-residue l.1.1.1 segment from the biological comparison and reports absence of homology warnings in both releases. Uses the retrieved family comment and the 2.08 lineages of d2quoa_ and d1w99a3, and notes the comment's SID predates the chain B rename to d1nqdb1, a useful identifier observation. States that structural core and topology plus the published analysis carry the inference because sequence similarity is negligible, that no alignment was run, that the 2.04 separation was not evidence of independent origin, and that no ligand, specificity or toxicity transfer is licensed. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

All classifications, sunids, boundaries, comments and the hf definition match the evidence. Clearly separates sequence-based homology (down to protein/species) from the broken fold inference; rejects coordinate/helix-packing/DNA-interface transfer; handles label noise, leakage, stratification and release pinning; declines quality ranking without retrieved SPACI records and states structural limits honestly. Does not identify mutations or method but does not claim to.

All must_include met: homology retained at family level with fold-alone caveat; fr flag explained via 99 SEQRES vs 50 ATOM residues and alignment/score bias; complete unflagged domain as representative, fragment kept as member with labelled SEQRES-level use and excluded from structural variability stats. Lineage sunids, boundaries, fr/cr9 annotations and quality values (1o5d XRAY 2.05 A SPACI 0.287; 1uc6 NMR 0.0216) all match bundle. Correctly notes SPACI is entry-level and cannot override fragment flag; rejects function/ligand transfer. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Complete: new superfamily in existing fold as absence of a positive homology claim, not a claim of analogy; family in existing superfamily asserts probable ancestry with a closer grouping; new fold contradicts observed similarity unless core differs; placement is a release-specific, revisable hypothesis requiring integrated evidence and manual curation. d.58 example (sunid 54861, class d description, d.58.1/5/6/7) supported by bundle; release metadata supported.

Correct hierarchy with sunids, current-release context, homology record (sf scope, no warnings) and annotations all bundle-supported. Correctly interprets the ATP-grasp/PIPK comment as similarity only and notes separate superfamilies are not negative evidence. Supports remote common ancestry and generic phosphotransfer mechanism, refuses transfer of substrate, regulation, inhibitor sensitivity, or activity. Evidence list covers same-family relationship, structure-based alignment of catalytic/specificity/regulatory residues, domain context, experiments, and literature.
